timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Welcome to ITU Telecom World 2017 here in Pusano, the Republic of Korea. I'm very pleased
to be joined in the studio today by Mr. Abraham Coffee Asante, who is CEO of the Ghana Investment
Fund for Electronic Communications. Mr Asante, thank you for having me.
Now I'd like to start off by talking about smart digital transformation as the theme of
this year's ITU Telecom World. What does it mean to you?
Yeah, well, smart digital transformation. I consider it as a digital transformation that
is supposed to make life convenient for the citizens of this world. And not in our part
of the world where we want to digitize because we've been in the analog field for some
time. And now there's a need for us to move rapidly, transforming into the digital age
and using them to our advantage to create opportunities for people to live better.
And what are the biggest challenges in your opinion and opportunities for smart technologies
over the next five years, let's say?
I think the biggest challenge that I see is that I haven't designed and implemented
some systems already that are on the ground. And now trying to digitize, there's the need
for us to look at a lot of events and resources. Financial resources, human resources, we need
to look at all these things and also to establish the understanding that we make businesses
now look at how they can transform by moving on to digital devices, making them available
for the citizens, making sure that the business community have got the necessary resources
for them to take up digitization. And these challenges are things that we look at. Some
of them really involve financial resources and have deep pockets before you'll be able
to realize it fully. But I believe that we can move from one step to the other based on
face to face movement and we'll get there.
And in terms of the projects that you're involved, we perhaps you could tell us a little
bit about the projects that are looking at digital services.
In respect to digital services, in Ghana, we first of all looking at how we can put
in the infrastructure for Wi-Fi and provide government services to the people.
It governs the way that we're going to provide good governance and also to provide public services.
In the area of business, we need to also try to help those who want to put in stackups
and those who want to transform. At least look at how we'll be able to make those who provide
devices for these people have it easy for them to provide. And also those who want to procure
their devices also have a leeway in trying to get them so that incrementally we'll be able
to get all these devices in place and also move faster because these technologies moving
very fast. And if you are slow, you'll be bitten. We need to move fast. We need to encourage
up. And then also putting the policies that will make them work.
Very inspiring words there. I wanted to ask you finally in terms of your attendance here
at ISU Telecom World, why is it important to attend this event? And has anything particularly
inspired you? Has anything made you think?
One of the things that I look at, I've been to most of the high level forum discussions.
I've seen how the SMEs are on the ground. I've gone to the shows. And I think it's a
common platform of bringing people in government, people in the area of providing the business
people who are also in the area of industry. All of us on one platform. It's an international
platform where we are trying to coordinate. And I believe that with this kind of coordination,
we will be able to make the world better sooner than later.
Abraham Coffin, thank you very much indeed.
Thank you.
Most welcome. I'm grateful for the opportunity.
